**Verdict: don't publish yet. One claim needs to change.**

**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Tea Subscription UK" | Descriptive, no claim |
| "Monthly loose leaf tea" | Product fact, fine |
| "If your box isn't right, we'll make it right" | **Unsupported** |
| "Free UK delivery on orders over £25" | Allowlisted (shipping policy) |

**Problem**

"If your box isn't right, we'll make it right" is a satisfaction guarantee in soft wording. It promises a remedy (replacement, refund, or something else) for any dissatisfaction. The brand policy has no such offer and says we never make guarantees of this kind. It also commits the business to something customer service hasn't signed up to, and the landing page would have to make the same promise.

**Compliant version**

> Headline: Tea Subscription UK
> Description: Monthly loose leaf tea. Pause or cancel any time. Free UK delivery on orders over £25.

The description is 86 characters. "Pause or cancel any time" comes from the allowlisted subscription terms claim. Before it runs, confirm that the landing page also states the free delivery threshold and the pause/cancel terms. Sam needs to approve it, as with all public content.

**Notes**
- The headline is 19 characters. You gave no character limit, so check the description against your platform's limit (Google RSA descriptions are 90).
- If you want a returns or "make it right" promise in ads, the product team needs to add it to the policy first, with the exact terms.

```json
{"issues": [{"quote": "If your box isn't right, we'll make it right.", "type": "guarantee"}], "publish": false}
```
